title: Cut and publish 0.6.1 carrying the LCLI-474 log.md fix
description:
Cut and publish 0.6.1, carrying LCLI-474 (lore sync destroys log.md entries it cannot
re-derive). Authorized by the user on 2026-09-11 after the orchestrator established that
every fleet session runs the published npm binary, so the fix reaches nobody until it
ships. quest-cli's standing ruling to hand-revert its log.md on every sync stays in force
until this release is on npm.

SCOPE: 0.6.0 -> 0.6.1, a single-purpose patch. dev was level with main before this work,
and Unreleased holds exactly one entry, so the release carries the LCLI-474 fix, the
LCLI-473 tracker record, and nothing else.

The bump is not a version string. Per docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md it is ONE commit
containing all of:
- seven package.json versions (root + six npm/<platform>/) AND the root's six
  optionalDependencies pins. release.yml's verify-versions job gates build on all seven
  plus the pin and the license/author/repository metadata.
- .claude-plugin/plugin.json's version. 0.4.3 shipped without this and the marketplace pin
  moving to v0.4.3 still resolved as 0.4.2 everywhere, because Claude Code reads
  plugin.json's own version, not the git tag.
- bun.lock regenerated with the PINNED Bun from .bun-version (1.3.14; the local toolchain
  matches, verified). A lockfile still resolving the previous version fails
  --frozen-lockfile in setup-bun and kills every CI job before any gate runs. The trap is
  that it does not fail at bump time -- the new platform packages do not exist on the
  registry yet, so the drift is invisible until publication makes the pins resolvable
  (LCLI-369).
- three Ladybug digest baselines, which move because the canonical export embeds
  lore/<version> as provenance. Only canonicalExportSha256 may move; if
  sourceInventorySha256 or taskSnapshotSha256 also moved, that is a code regression
  wearing a version bump's commit message. A negative control (revert only the root
  version, expect the OLD baselines to pass) proves the change is version-driven.
- README install commands stay versionless, and docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md is
  the ONE file in docs/ carrying the current published version. The grep sweep for
  '@opum-ai/lore@[0-9]' must return only its two pinned historical exemptions.

THEN: promote dev to main (PR, full main matrix on that exact SHA, then git push origin
dev:main -- never the merge button), tag the verified commit, dispatch Release with
publish: false, and publish THAT RUN'S npm-packages artifact via
scripts/publish-release.sh -- platform packages first, root last, never a locally rebuilt
tarball.

TWO STEPS NEED THE USER DIRECTLY and are batched into one ask rather than trickled: the
annotated tag (git tag -a is classifier-denied in this session) and the npm publish itself.
Both are irreversible; a published version cannot be unpublished, only deprecated.

DOWNSTREAM OBLIGATION, easy to forget because nothing in this repo fails without it:
opum-marketplace's check-federated-content.mjs asserts the federated skills/ bytes match a
baseline resolved from the tag. A new tag without telling opum-marketplace the resolved
skills/ SHA turns its check red.

acceptanceCriteria.text: All seven package.json versions, the six optionalDependencies pins, and .claude-plugin/plugin.json read 0.6.1, in one commit
bun.lock regenerated with the Bun pinned in .bun-version, and `bun install --frozen-lockfile` exits 0 with its exit code taken unpiped
The three Ladybug digest baselines are refreshed, and the change is PROVEN version-driven: only canonicalExportSha256 moved, and the negative control returns to passing against the old baselines
The docs sweep for '@opum-ai/lore@[0-9]' returns only its two pinned historical exemptions; release-truth carries the new version and no other file grew a current-state claim
dev is promoted to main by fast-forward (git push origin dev:main) after the full matrix is green on that exact SHA, never via the merge button
The tag points at the verified commit, and Release is dispatched with publish: false on it

The seven published tarballs are the workflow run's own npm-packages artifact, sha256-verified by scripts/publish-release.sh before any registry write, platform packages first and the root package last
opum-marketplace is told the resolved skills/ SHA for the new tag, so its federated-content check does not go red
quest-cli is told when 0.6.1 is on npm, since its ruling to hand-revert log.md stands until then

implementationNotes:

Checked as of this note: no v0.6.1 tag on origin, npm still serves 0.6.0 latest. Nothing else is blocking -- dev/main are level, all nine acceptance criteria are ready to check the moment the registry confirms 0.6.1, and no PR is open because there is nothing left to review; the remaining work is entirely the user executing commands already in hand.

Monitored npm hourly for three hours after handing over the sequence, then stopped re-arming deliberately -- an indeterminate wait on human timing does not warrant indefinite hourly polling. Will resume from either the tag appearing or npm showing 0.6.1, whichever is noticed first, and will check all nine criteria + close the task in this same record once confirmed. If a future sweep or session finds this In Progress with nothing else changed, that is expected, not a defect -- ask the user directly rather than re-deriving this from the repo state.
finalSummary:
MAIN VERIFIED, 2026-09-12: promoted via git push origin dev:main (fast-forward, PR #9 closed unmerged per its own by-design promotion-is-manual refusal, then auto-marked MERGED by GitHub once the commits reached main). main is 92351723c8f4d14826ce846f1573ac170a6df3ee.

Full main CI matrix on that SHA: 12 success, 1 skipped (promotion is manual -- correctly skipped, since that job's condition is pull_request-only and this is a push). One transient finding, resolved: lint-typecheck-test (macos-latest) was CANCELLED at its 20-minute job timeout on the first run -- lint and typecheck passed, only Test was cut off. Prior main runs took 2m15s-2m51s for the same job, so this was an ~8x outlier, not a marginal timeout, and worth distrusting rather than assuming benign. Re-ran: passed clean in 1m33s, back in the normal range. Treated as runner degradation, not a defect in this change -- confirmed rather than assumed, since macOS is the one platform PRs never exercise and this was its first run of this code.
